s1.syndrome_frame: Acute vision loss in one eye following a traumatic incident to the head
salient_findings: Decreased vision in one eye after being struck by lightning
Central macular thickening on fundus examination at 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract visible in the affected eye at 7 weeks
key_facts: Patient is a white woman in her 20s
Unremarkable medical and ocular history
Symptoms began 4 days prior to presentation
Struck by lightning directly to the forehead
Uncorrected visual acuity measured 20/50 OD and 20/20 OS
Pupils were symmetric with no relative afferent pupillary defect
Initial anterior segment examination was normal
Initial dilated fundus examination showed no apparent abnormalities
Central macular thickening developed by 2 weeks
Mild posterior subcapsular cataract developed by 7 weeks
Spectral-domain OCT showed subtle irregularity of outer retinal layers initially
Intraretinal cystoid changes and subfoveal ellipsoid zone disruption developed by 2 weeks

shortlist.label: Purtscher-like retinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Trauma to the head and eye symptoms match this condition

shortlist.label: Commotio retinae
shortlist.why_kept: Blunt trauma to the head and subsequent vision loss are consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
shortlist.why_kept: Direct lightning strike to the forehead could cause optic nerve damage

shortlist.label: Cystoid macular edema
shortlist.why_kept: Spectral-domain OCT findings of intraretinal cystoid changes support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Lightning-induced chorioretinopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Direct lightning strike and subsequent retinal changes are consistent with this rare condition

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and findings, including decreased vision after a traumatic event, normal initial anterior segment examination, and development of central macular thickening and intraretinal cystoid changes, are consistent with Purtscher-like retinopathy, which is a rare condition associated with traumatic injuries and can cause retinal damage without direct ocular trauma.

rejected.label: Commotio retinae
rejected.why: Commotio retinae typically presents with immediate vision loss and retinal edema, which does not match the delayed onset of symptoms in this case.

rejected.label: Traumatic optic neuropathy
rejected.why: Traumatic optic neuropathy would likely present with a relative afferent pupillary defect, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Cystoid macular edema
rejected.why: While cystoid macular edema is present, it is not the primary diagnosis that explains the overall clinical picture, including the traumatic cause and the pattern of retinal damage.

rejected.label: Lightning-induced chorioretinopathy
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the case to suggest a direct effect of lightning on the choroid or retina beyond the traumatic mechanism.
